what: New video shows man believed to be Tyler Robinson before Charlie Kirk shooting

clean_source_blocks.text: A new video, released on Sunday local time, was captured by a door security camera at a home in Orem, Utah. The door camera films a grey Dodge Challenger driving past on the morning of Kirk’s death. Local police said they believe the suspected shooter drove the same car prior to the shooting, according to Fox News. More than an hour later, the footage appears to show Robinson, dressed in a dark red t-shirt, shorts and a backpack, walking past the home in the opposite direction. Robinson did not have any prior criminal record before the alleged murder of Kirk. In a press conference with Utah Governor Spencer Cox on Thursday night local time, footage and images were released of a man, dressed in all-dark clothing, running along a university roof before dropping to the ground.

New footage has been released showing alleged gunman Tyler Robinson on the morning he is said to have shot and killed conservative influencer Charlie Kirk. Kirk, 31, was fatally shot in the neck during a speaking event at Utah Valley University last Wednesday. A large police response followed with more than 7000 leads and tips from the public, the largest number the FBI has received on an incident since the Boston Marathon bombing in 2013, the bureau said. Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today Robinson, 22, was reportedly recognised by his father in videos and photos shared by news outlets of the alleged gunman and urged his son to hand himself in. A tip to police from a family friend ultimately lead to Robinson, an electrical apprentice, handing himself in on Friday.

PROVO, Utah (AP) — The man charged with killing Charlie Kirk strolled Utah Valley University in shorts and a T-shirt, bought a meal at Chick-fil-A and made contact with people from Kirk’s organization, before returning in different clothes to shoot the conservative activist from a rooftop, an investigator testified Tuesday. Former State Bureau of Investigation Agent David Hull described Tyler Robinson’s alleged movements before and after Kirk was killed as prosecutors played previously unseen campus surveillance videos in state court. The defendant first arrived on campus about four hours before the shooting, Hull said. Prosecutors say they intend to seek the death penalty in the case. They are trying to convince Judge Tony Graf that they have enough evidence to bring Robinson to trial on an aggravated murder charge.

The figure is believed to have run towards a wooded area before disappearing. Authorities said the suspect, now believed to be Robinson, was wearing sunglasses, Converse shoes and a black T-shirt featuring an American flag and an eagle. The governor called the shooter an “evil human being” before saying legal work was being done behind the scenes to pursue the death penalty. However, Utah Attorney General Derek Brown told local television station ABC4 he couldn’t say whether prosecutors will pursue the death penalty for Kirk’s murder, but that “everything is on the table”. Talking to CNN, Cox said Robinson was not cooperating with authorities and had not confessed to the shooting. He is expected to be formally charged on Tuesday, according to Cox. ---

original_article.research:
[Lähde: 7NEWS Australia]
New footage has been released showing alleged gunman Tyler Robinson on the morning he is said to have shot and killed conservative influencer Charlie Kirk.

Kirk, 31, was fatally shot in the neck during a speaking event at Utah Valley University last Wednesday.

A large police response followed with more than 7000 leads and tips from the public, the largest number the FBI has received on an incident since the Boston Marathon bombing in 2013, the bureau said.

Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today

Robinson, 22, was reportedly recognised by his father in videos and photos shared by news outlets of the alleged gunman and urged his son to hand himself in.

A tip to police from a family friend ultimately lead to Robinson, an electrical apprentice, handing himself in on Friday.

A new video, released on Sunday local time, was captured by a door security camera at a home in Orem, Utah.

The door camera films a grey Dodge Challenger driving past on the morning of Kirk’s death.

Local police said they believe the suspected shooter drove the same car prior to the shooting, according to Fox News.

More than an hour later, the footage appears to show Robinson, dressed in a dark red t-shirt, shorts and a backpack, walking past the home in the opposite direction.

Robinson did not have any prior criminal record before the alleged murder of Kirk.

In a press conference with Utah Governor Spencer Cox on Thursday night local time, footage and images were released of a man, dressed in all-dark clothing, running along a university roof before dropping to the ground.

The figure is believed to have run towards a wooded area before disappearing.

Authorities said the suspect, now believed to be Robinson, was wearing sunglasses, Converse shoes and a black T-shirt featuring an American flag and an eagle.

The governor called the shooter an “evil human being” before saying legal work was being done behind the scenes to pursue the death penalty.

However, Utah Attorney General Derek Brown told local television station ABC4 he couldn’t say whether prosecutors will pursue the death penalty for Kirk’s murder, but that “everything is on the table”.

Talking to CNN, Cox said Robinson was not cooperating with authorities and had not confessed to the shooting.

He is expected to be formally charged on Tuesday, according to Cox.

---

[Lähde: Boston Herald]
PROVO, Utah (AP) — The man charged with killing Charlie Kirk strolled Utah Valley University in shorts and a T-shirt, bought a meal at Chick-fil-A and made contact with people from Kirk’s organization, before returning in different clothes to shoot the conservative activist from a rooftop, an investigator testified Tuesday.

Former State Bureau of Investigation Agent David Hull described Tyler Robinson’s alleged movements before and after Kirk was killed as prosecutors played previously unseen campus surveillance videos in state court. The defendant first arrived on campus about four hours before the shooting, Hull said.

Prosecutors say they intend to seek the death penalty in the case. They are trying to convince Judge Tony Graf that they have enough evidence to bring Robinson to trial on an aggravated murder charge.

Robinson has not yet entered a plea. His attorneys have not commented on his guilt or innocence. They have, however, sought to get the death penalty taken off the table, so far unsuccessfully.

In a video shown Tuesday, Robinson climbs over a railing onto a rooftop, crouches down and runs to a site overlooking where Kirk was speaking, Hull testified. After the shooting, Robinson runs back across the roof, drops to the ground and flees on foot, Hull said.

Investigators found the suspected murder weapon — a bolt-action rifle with one spent round — wrapped in a towel in some nearby woods. Later that night, a police offer again spotted Robinson in the campus area, Hull testified.

This week’s preliminary hearing marks the most significant presentation of evidence to date in the case. Authorities allege Robinson, 23, shot Kirk on Sept. 10 while the 31-year-old activist and ally of President Donald Trump was speaking to a crowd of thousands.

Defense attorney Kathryn Nester questioned Hull’s handling of the crime scene on the day of the shooting. She also asked about a bullet that was found on campus at a different location than the alleged shooting site.

Hull said that bullet was traced back to a law enforcement officer who had “cleared” his weapon, ejecting an unused bullet. He also said a handgun in a backpack was found at the scene.

Prosecutors contend the shooting endangered others at Kirk’s campus event — an aggravating circumstance that could make the crime punishable by death under Utah law. Robinson also faces possible sentence enhancements based on the prosecution’s claim that he targeted Kirk because of his political views.

payload.title: Uudet videot näyttävät Tyler Robinsonin epäiltyjä liikkeitä ennen Charlie Kirkin ampumista
payload.summary: Oikeudessa esitetyt ja viranomaisten aiemmin julkaisemat videot kuvaavat Tyler Robinsoniksi epäillyn miehen liikkeitä Utahissa ennen konservatiivivaikuttaja Charlie Kirkin kuolemaan johtanutta ampumista.
payload.content:
Tyler Robinsonin epäiltyjä liikkeitä ennen konservatiivivaikuttaja Charlie Kirkin ampumista on kuvattu uusilla valvontavideoilla, joita on esitetty oikeudessa Utahissa. Tutkijan mukaan Robinson saapui Utah Valley Universityn kampukselle tunteja ennen ampumista, liikkui alueella arkivaatteissa ja palasi myöhemmin eri vaatteissa ennen kuin Kirk ammuttiin kuoliaaksi puhetilaisuudessa.

## Valvontavideot kuvaavat liikkeitä ennen ampumista

Entinen Utahin osavaltion tutkintaviraston agentti David Hull kuvasi oikeudessa Robinsonin väitettyjä liikkeitä ennen ampumista ja sen jälkeen. Syyttäjät esittivät osavaltion tuomioistuimessa aiemmin näkemättömiä kampuksen valvontatallenteita.

Hullin mukaan Robinson saapui kampukselle noin neljä tuntia ennen ampumista. Hänen kerrottiin liikkuneen alueella shortseissa ja t-paidassa, ostaneen ruokaa Chick-fil-A-ravintolasta ja olleen yhteydessä Kirkin järjestön ihmisiin. Syyttäjien mukaan hän palasi myöhemmin eri vaatteissa ja ampui Kirkin katolta.

Kirk, 31, ammuttiin kuolettavasti kaulaan puhetilaisuuden aikana Utah Valley Universityssä. Tapauksen jälkeen käynnistyi laaja poliisioperaatio, ja FBI:n mukaan yleisöltä saatiin yli 7 000 vihjettä. Virasto kuvasi määrää suurimmaksi yksittäiseen tapaukseen liittyväksi vihjemääräksi sitten vuoden 2013 Bostonin maratonpommi-iskun.

## Epäilty antautui poliisille

Oremissa Utahissa sijaitsevan kodin ovikamera tallensi ampumispäivän aamuna harmaan Dodge Challengerin ajavan ohi. Paikallisen poliisin mukaan epäillyn ampujan uskotaan ajaneen samaa autoa ennen ampumista. Yli tuntia myöhemmin samalla tallenteella näkyy henkilö, jonka uskotaan olevan Robinson, kulkemassa talon ohi vastakkaiseen suuntaan tummanpunaisessa t-paidassa, shortseissa ja reppu selässään.

Viranomaiset ovat julkaisseet myös kuvia ja videota tummiin vaatteisiin pukeutuneesta miehestä, joka juoksee yliopiston katolla ja pudottautuu maahan. Hahmon uskotaan paenneen kohti metsäistä aluetta. Viranomaisten mukaan epäilty käytti aurinkolaseja, Converse-kenkiä ja mustaa t-paitaa, jossa oli Yhdysvaltain lippu ja kotka.

Robinson, 22, antautui poliisille perjantaina. Hänen isänsä kerrotaan tunnistaneen hänet tiedotusvälineiden julkaisemista kuvista ja videoista ja kehottaneen häntä antautumaan. Perhetuttavan poliisille antama vihje johti lopulta Robinsoniin. Utahin kuvernööri Spencer Coxin mukaan Robinson ei ole tehnyt tunnustusta eikä tee yhteistyötä viranomaisten kanssa.

Syyttäjät ovat ilmoittaneet aikovansa hakea kuolemanrangaistusta. Utahin oikeusministeri Derek Brown sanoi kuitenkin paikalliselle televisiokanavalle, ettei hän voi vahvistaa, aikovatko syyttäjät vaatia sitä Kirkin murhasta, mutta kaikki vaihtoehdot ovat pöydällä. Syyttäjät pyrkivät vakuuttamaan tuomari Tony Grafin siitä, että Robinsonia vastaan on riittävästi näyttöä törkeää murhaa koskevan oikeudenkäynnin aloittamiseksi.
summary_bullets: Oikeudessa on esitetty valvontavideoita Tyler Robinsonin epäillyistä liikkeistä ennen Charlie Kirkin ampumista.
Tutkijan mukaan Robinson saapui kampukselle noin neljä tuntia ennen ampumista ja palasi myöhemmin eri vaatteissa.
Robinson antautui poliisille perjantaina perhetuttavan vihjeen jälkeen, eikä viranomaisten mukaan ole tunnustanut.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketissa olleisiin viranomaisten, oikeuskäsittelyn ja uutislähteiden kuvaamiin tietoihin. Muotoilussa on säilytetty epäiltyä koskeva varovaisuus, koska asia on oikeudessa kesken.

Robinson antautui poliisille perjantaina perhetuttavan vihjeen jälkeen, eikä viranomaisten mukaan ole tunnustanut.
article.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketissa olleisiin viranomaisten, oikeuskäsittelyn ja uutislähteiden kuvaamiin tietoihin. Muotoilussa on säilytetty epäiltyä koskeva varovaisuus, koska asia on oikeudessa kesken.
article.source_text:
A new video, released on Sunday local time, was captured by a door security camera at a home in Orem, Utah. The door camera films a grey Dodge Challenger driving past on the morning of Kirk’s death. Local police said they believe the suspected shooter drove the same car prior to the shooting, according to Fox News. More than an hour later, the footage appears to show Robinson, dressed in a dark red t-shirt, shorts and a backpack, walking past the home in the opposite direction. Robinson did not have any prior criminal record before the alleged murder of Kirk. In a press conference with Utah Governor Spencer Cox on Thursday night local time, footage and images were released of a man, dressed in all-dark clothing, running along a university roof before dropping to the ground.

New footage has been released showing alleged gunman Tyler Robinson on the morning he is said to have shot and killed conservative influencer Charlie Kirk. Kirk, 31, was fatally shot in the neck during a speaking event at Utah Valley University last Wednesday. A large police response followed with more than 7000 leads and tips from the public, the largest number the FBI has received on an incident since the Boston Marathon bombing in 2013, the bureau said. Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today Robinson, 22, was reportedly recognised by his father in videos and photos shared by news outlets of the alleged gunman and urged his son to hand himself in. A tip to police from a family friend ultimately lead to Robinson, an electrical apprentice, handing himself in on Friday.

PROVO, Utah (AP) — The man charged with killing Charlie Kirk strolled Utah Valley University in shorts and a T-shirt, bought a meal at Chick-fil-A and made contact with people from Kirk’s organization, before returning in different clothes to shoot the conservative activist from a rooftop, an investigator testified Tuesday. Former State Bureau of Investigation Agent David Hull described Tyler Robinson’s alleged movements before and after Kirk was killed as prosecutors played previously unseen campus surveillance videos in state court. The defendant first arrived on campus about four hours before the shooting, Hull said. Prosecutors say they intend to seek the death penalty in the case. They are trying to convince Judge Tony Graf that they have enough evidence to bring Robinson to trial on an aggravated murder charge.

The figure is believed to have run towards a wooded area before disappearing. Authorities said the suspect, now believed to be Robinson, was wearing sunglasses, Converse shoes and a black T-shirt featuring an American flag and an eagle. The governor called the shooter an “evil human being” before saying legal work was being done behind the scenes to pursue the death penalty. However, Utah Attorney General Derek Brown told local television station ABC4 he couldn’t say whether prosecutors will pursue the death penalty for Kirk’s murder, but that “everything is on the table”. Talking to CNN, Cox said Robinson was not cooperating with authorities and had not confessed to the shooting. He is expected to be formally charged on Tuesday, according to Cox. ---
